items.message: The diff matches its description: `--eject` is removed, `show-workflow` is added, and REGISTER_TAIL's comment is updated to point to the new command. The change does less import-merging work than before (`_wrap_long_imports`, `_ejected_source`, `_without_duplicate_imports` path for eject all gone), which is consistent with the stated rationale.

The `_workflow_ids` helper extracts workflow ids by running a regex over `inspect.getsource(module.register)`. The PR description relies on this being reliable, and `test_the_id_discovery_is_not_vacuous` guards against the regex going silent — but the regex matches `workflow(id="...")` only in its current single-line form. If `ruff format` or a future edit splits the call across lines, the regex returns an empty set silently. The test for vacuousness pins the exact current id set, so it would ca…[truncated]

Undocumented behaviour: `show-workflow --registered` calls `_default_lockstep()` as a side effect to force registration. This is noted in an inline comment but not in the command's docstring. A user reading `--registered` will not know that `_default_lockstep()` must run for the flag to work, and if that function has side effects (file I/O, network, etc.) those are invisible at the CLI help level. This is minor but is a gap between what the flag says and what it does.

The test `test_ejecting_gives_the_source_back_and_it_is_the_source_that_runs` is replaced by `test_the_shipped_process_can_be_read_without_being_copied` and companions. The new tests cover listing, single-id, full-family, `--registered`, and error paths. No coverage gap is apparent for the paths added in this diff.
